modeReason: Two stories reached well above the fresh threshold of 8: buyers paying a premium for human-made art (novelty 3 x magnitude 2 x breadth 2 = 12) and new research that brief AI use weakens persistence (3 x 2 x 2 = 12), both genuinely new angles not covered in recent days.
phrase: People now pay more for art made by a human. New research found that ten minutes of AI help can weaken someone's ability to keep trying.
phraseAlternatives: A report found people now pay more for art stamped not AI. A separate study found ten minutes of AI help can weaken someone's drive to keep trying.
Shoppers now pay extra for art made without AI. Researchers warn that a short dose of AI help can quietly weaken someone's will to finish hard things.
Human-made art is now worth more, buyers say. A new study finds that AI shortcuts can make it harder for people to keep trying on their own.

brief.concept: A shopper pays a premium for a hand-signed painting, while beside them a person reaching for the last piece of a puzzle watches a robot arm place it first.
brief.metaphor: People now pay more for human effort, even as AI quietly takes away the small struggles that build it.

cast.who: a shopper holding out coins for a hand-signed painting
a framed painting with a small human handprint signature, labeled NOT AI
a person reaching toward a nearly finished jigsaw puzzle
a chatbot robot arm sliding the puzzle's last piece into place first

brief.composition: A riso duotone diptych split by a thin vertical line, blue and fluorescent pink inks on cream paper. Left half: a shopper offers coins across a small counter toward a framed painting with a simple handprint signature and a small label reading NOT AI. Right half: a seated person's hand reaches for a nearly complete puzzle just as a robot arm slips in the last piece first; a small meter beside them dips low. Two shapes per half, flat color fills, only the words NOT AI appear on the image.
brief.alt: A shopper pays coins for a hand-signed painting labeled not ai. Beside them, a person reaching for the last puzzle piece watches a robot arm place it there first.
